Notes to Appendix B
1. Yeats's friend Edmund Dulac had previously composed some music for the
play At the Hawk's Well.
 The body of the song is a version of An Smachdaoin Cr6n, variously translated
as "The Little Brown Mallet" or "The Copper-colored Stick of Tobacco." The
use of the final musical phrase as a chorus is not traditional.
 3· The song is that provided by Richard Michael Levey (1811-99) for the lyric
"Limerick is Beautiful" in the play The Colleen Bawn by Dion Boucicault
( 182o-go). Levey's song is a 6/8 version of Ftiinne Geal an Lae, usually trans-
lated as "The Dawning of the Day."
 4· The song is a loose adaptation of Bruach na Carraige Baine, literally "The
Brink of the White Rock" but usually known as "To Plough the Rocks of
Bawn." The addition to the chorus is not traditional.

as brief a compass as possible. Annotation of other kinds, as well as interpretive
commentary, has been avoided. Thus, for example, information on Yeats's sources
has usually been offered only when Yeats called attention to them (whether in
the poem or in a note), as with "Imitated from the Japanese" (poem 323). Cross-
references to Yeats's other works or lo his correspondence are given only when
such material provides a particularly concise annotation. Unnamed individuals
